:::::: bs-page-shell
::::: bs-reading-column
Backgammon Simplified is an open-source project for understanding the game and making better decisions.

The idea is simple:

> **Come with a question. Leave with a clear mental model you can use at the board.**

We try to make difficult ideas clearer, build useful tools, and help more people get excited about backgammon.

## Why We Built This

I started this project while trying to understand my own blunders. The engine gave me the best moves. A friend who is a great player said, "Eventually, you'll start to see it."

I wanted to know what I was supposed to see, as I asked questions like:

::: bs-question-examples
[\>]{.bs-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *Why is 25% often called the take point... and yet it rarely ever is?*

[\>]{.bs-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *When should I run a lone back checker, move it up, or leave it where it is?*

[\>]{.bs-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *Why is breaking an anchor brilliant one game and a blunder the next?*

[\>]{.bs-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *What can one position teach me about the thousands I'll see later?*

[// goal: clarity over perfection]{.bs-code-note}
:::

Backgammon Simplified is my attempt to answer questions with real positions, clear explanations, and evidence instead of folklore.

::: bs-section-heading
## Introducing Marty Gale

[ROLE: AUTHOR :: RESEARCHER :: PLAYER]{.bs-heading-meta}
:::

Hi, I'm **Marty Gale, PhD**.[^1]

I research the intersection of dice rigging, probability, and questionable doubling decisions.

Behind the joke, Marty Gale is the public author identity for this project.

I am not presenting myself as one of the world's great backgammon players. I am a curious player learning in public: asking questions, testing ideas, making mistakes, and trying to leave behind explanations that are more useful than a table of rollout results.
